description: An ADSR envelope with a modulation input for each stage in four modulation modes, per-stage level and gate outputs, force-advance triggers and a sample-and-hold on the output

params.text: Forces the envelope on to the next stage while it is held
Steps that stage's level output between the plain envelope and the envelope with its modulation, shown by a blue lamp for the modulated one
Steps the decay level output through the plain envelope, the envelope with its modulation, and the envelope with the sustain level subtracted, shown by a blue and then a green lamp
Attenuates and inverts that stage's modulation input, from -0.2 to 0.2, before the modulation mode applies it
Sets the length of the attack, the phasor step being 0.000315 raised to this power, so turning it up makes the stage longer
Sets the length of the decay, the phasor step being 0.000315 raised to this power, so turning it up makes the stage longer
Sets the level the envelope holds at while the gate stays high, 0 to 1
Sets the length of the release, the phasor step being 0.000315 raised to this power, so turning it up makes the stage longer
Steps that stage's modulation mode on: Ring, Add, Add With Fade, or Inverse Envelope Addition, shown as red, green, blue and white on the lamp beside it
Steps the sustain stage's modulation mode between Ring and Add, shown as red and green on the lamp beside it
Bends the attack, the linear ramp being raised to this power, from 0.2 for a fast rise to 3 for a slow one
Bends the decay by moving the control point of a quadratic curve between the peak and the sustain level
Bends the release, the ramp being raised to this power, from 0.2 for a fast fall to 7.4 for a slow one
Attenuates the global ring input, from 0 to 0.2, before it is added to the offset knob around it
Scales both main outputs, from silence to full; with the global ring jack patched it becomes the offset added to the attenuated ring signal
Sets how much of each stage's modulation is crossfaded into the next, to keep the modulation from clicking at a stage boundary
Slews the main outputs towards the held value instead of stepping to it, which turns the sample-and-hold into a track-and-hold
Sets the rate of the internal sample-and-hold clock on the main outputs; at the fully clockwise setting of 40 the outputs update every sample and no holding happens

inputs.text: A voltage of 5V or more forces the envelope on to the next stage
The modulation signal for that stage, which the stage's attenuator and mode apply to the envelope; an empty jack falls back to the nearest patched stage above it
A rising edge starts the envelope at the attack; the envelope falls into release when this goes low during sustain, and it reads high above 1V
Multiplies both main outputs after every other modulation, scaled by the small attenuator knob and added to the offset around it
A rising edge restarts the envelope at the attack without waiting for the gate to fall
Slows the internal sample-and-hold clock as its voltage rises, the rate being the knob setting times one minus a tenth of this voltage
Lowers the crossfade setting as its voltage rises, a tenth of the voltage being subtracted from the anger figure

outputs.text: That stage's own envelope segment, 0-10V, plain or with its modulation according to the button beside it
Carries 10V while the envelope is in that stage and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while the envelope is in the release, or a trigger at the moment the envelope finishes when the menu is set that way
The finished envelope, scaled by the offset knob and clipped to ±12V
The finished envelope inverted, scaled by the offset knob and clipped to ±12V, or the plain envelope when the menu is set that way

notes: with only the gate patched and only the plus output taken, it behaves as an ordinary ADSR; everything else is modulation laid on top of that
going from attack to decay always starts the decay at 10V, and the release always starts from the sustain level, whether or not the sustain stage happened
the modulation inputs normal downwards, so a cable in the attack modulation jack feeds every stage below it that has no cable of its own
both main outputs are hard clipped at ±12V, and the offset knob is the way to pull a heavily modulated envelope back under that ceiling
turning a stage's attenuator knob gives it the value of the attenuator above it as its default, so a double-click sets a row to match the row above
menu: Negative Out Dry — makes the minus output carry the plain unmodulated envelope in place of the inverted modulated one
Release Gate → EOR Trig — makes the release gate output a single trigger when the envelope finishes, in place of a gate lasting the release
Decrease Time — takes 0.1 off the attack, decay and release time knobs together
Increase Time — adds 0.1 to the attack, decay and release time knobs together
